title: Hosted inference behavioral PRD: scope adjustments, acceptance matrix and launch checklist
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Comprehensive PRD for behavioral guarantees and acceptance criteria for the consolidated hosted endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). This ticket defines minimal viable behavioral contracts, telemetry and rollout controls, documents two scope adjustments agreed in triage, and contains a launch checklist for cross-functional readiness.
background: We are unifying multiple hosted inference surfaces into a single predictable behavior set to reduce customer confusion and ease SDK support. Previous work focused on surface parity; this PRD focuses on behavioral guarantees (response shape, error semantics, quality SLOs) and the acceptance matrix customers/SEs rely on for migration.
goals: Define clear behavioral contracts per endpoint: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Specify acceptance tests and SLO thresholds for initial launch
Document rollout strategy (canary -> regional rollout) and fallbacks
Clarify scope changes and traceable decisions for stakeholders
non_goals: Not adding new model families in this launch (deferred)
No major SDK surface changes to existing client libraries (compatibility only)
No multi-tenant private deployment changes — Private/Dedicated handled separately
user_stories: As a product engineer, I need consistent error codes and retry guidance so my service can handle transient failures without user-visible regressions
As an ML platform owner, I need baseline latency and quality SLOs to estimate capacity and cost impact
As a solutions engineer, I need a deterministic embedding vector spec so downstream retrieval systems behave consistently
requirements: Behavior: chat and completions endpoints must return a structured response with stable 'id', 'model', 'choices' arrays and 'finish_reason' semantics
Embeddings: vectors must be L2-normalized at release and documented dimension must match model catalog
Rerank: API accepts a top-K list and returns stable scores in the same numeric range as the evaluation harness (0..1), deterministic ordering for equal scores preserved by input index
Error semantics: 4xx indicates customer input or model incompatibility; 5xx indicates infra issues. Retry-After header required on 429 and rate-limit responses
Telemetry: per-request token counts, model_variant, KV-cache-hit boolean, route_latency_ms, and sampling of full responses for eval must be included
SLOs: P95 latency <= 200ms for embeddings (small models), <= 350ms for chat/completions under normal load; availability >= 99.9% for hosted tier during launch window
acceptance_criteria: Automated suite green: 120 synthetic scenarios covering prompt edge cases for chat/completions and embeddings vector stability
Compatibility tests: existing SDK integration tests pass for customers using pinned model versions
Quality gate: eval harness (50 curated prompts) shows no more than 3% regression in relevance metrics versus baseline model variants
Observability: console dashboards show token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, error budget burn rate; alerts configured for error-rate > 0.5% over 5m
Canary criteria: initial canary at 2% traffic for 24h with SLOs met and no critical errors before 10% expansion
Fallback behavior: if model variant unavailable, traffic must failover to compatible variant within 5s without changing response shape
Security: KMS-integrated logging for sampled responses and access logs available to SOC for audit review
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood (Redwood apps) — 72h stability window
Phase 1: 2% public canary in us-west for 24h (metrics and SRE signoff required)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% over 48h with regional monitoring (us-west -> us-east)
Phase 3: 100% rollout regionally with 24h observation, then global expansion over 72h
Rollback: automatic rollback on error budget breach (>1% 5xx or >1.5x expected latency P95 sustained for 15m)
rollout_checklist: Endpoint contracts published to internal docs and SDK teams notified
E2E test harness updated in CI and green for all models in catalog
Console dashboards: per-route and per-model panels created and verified
Canary tokens and routing rules configured in control plane
Runbook and incident playbook published and acknowledged by SRE
Security review complete and sampling/PII redaction validated
Customer-facing migration notes drafted and staged for docs site
scope_changes: Scope Change A (2026-03-09): Removed multi-protocol (gRPC) initial launch due to SDK readiness — keep REST-only for launch. Rationale: SDK and client matrix not ready; reduces risk to canary metrics.

Scope Change B (2026-03-12): Added deterministic embedding normalization as mandatory (previously optional) after regression observed in downstream retrieval tests — trade-off: small compute cost increase but prevents semantic drift
decisions: Decision 1: Use 'finish_reason' values set {stop, length, timeout, error} and document mapping for SDKs — agreed by API and SDK leads
Decision 2: Canary cadence of 24h at 2% then 48h to 25% — chosen to capture diurnal traffic patterns across key regions
Decision 3: Defer adding model quantization profiles to initial hosted launch; Optimize will push recommendations post-launch
open_risks: Risk: Embedding dimensionality changes from upstream model onboarding could require urgent migration; mitigation: strict model gating and schema checks in catalog
Risk: Telemetry volume increase due to sampled full-response capture may bump retention costs; mitigation: sample rate capped at 0.5% and adjustable
Risk: SLOs under peak load if autoscaling config is underprovisioned; mitigation: run load tests at 2x expected peak before rollout
